text:
sara: Heads-up — this morning a keystore policy tweak in eu-west-1 caused a fraction of GPU nodes to fail decrypt during boot. Warm-pool instances started flapping and the autoscaler evicted ~18 nodes in the last 20m. logs: `keystore: decrypt error status=403 key=arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:...`

mike_sre: seeing the same in staging and prod canaries. Healthchecks failing at boot -> kubelet never registers, so ASG health replace kicks in. Warm pool dropped from ~120 -> ~95.

anika_sec: which policy change? I rolled out a conditional key policy to restrict cross-account assume-role for a couple of managed services last night. I thought we scoped it to tooling-prod only.

sara: policy change was the one anika mentioned. It looks like the keystore proxy (privnet-keystore) queues requests and returns 403 for decrypt on some node agent sessions. Full stack trace attached in logs.

devon_platform: quick datapoint — the failing nodes are all in the eu-west-1a az, on the same subnet behind a recently tightened firewall rule for egress to the keystore. Could be a race where keystore denies + conntrack exhaustion from retries.

kenny_oncall: I've paused the policy rollout in the control plane. anika, can you confirm rollback?

anika_sec: rolling back now. patch: `terraform apply -target=module.keystore.policy -var 'restrict_cross_account=false'` — kicking it off. ETA ~2m for propagation to keystore-proxy.

deploy-bot: canary rollback initiated by anika_sec — run 8/8 steps queued

mike_sre: while we wait, proposal: add a transient fallback in agent boot path to use cached bootstrap keys for up to 5m if keystore returns 403/5xx. That would avoid churn during policy transitions. Any objections?

devon_platform: +1. It's a small change to node-agent logic: if decrypt fails with auth errors, check `/var/lib/redwood/keystore-cache` then allow boot-if-cache-valid. We'll also need a telemetry flag to count these fallbacks.

lina_cost: just flagging cost impact — evicting 18 GPUs and re-provisioning burns warm-pool credits and increases on-demand start costs. Rough estimate ~ $2.4k extra this window. If we do frequent rollbacks that adds up.

anika_sec: rollback applied. Confirming proxy now returns 200 for decrypt requests. Please validate node boots.

mike_sre: nodes in eu-west-1a are now finishing bootstrap. Warm pool is back to ~118. No new evictions in the last 3m. Good catch.

kenny_oncall: next steps: 1) lifecycle patch for node-agent to consult keystore-cache during boot fallback (devon to own). 2) add a pre-rollout test in staging that flips a temporary deny to ensure fallback path works. 3) change firewall rollout playbook to avoid AZ-wide egress tighten at once (roll by subnet). 4) add alert for "keystore decrypt 403 spikey" tied to warm-pool drop.

devon_platform: I'll open the PR for the boot fallback and a canary test harness. Targeting hotfix branch: `platform/node-agent#hotfix/keystore-boot-fallback`. Will include metrics: `node.keystore.boot_fallback_count` and `node.boot_latency`.

anika_sec: we'll also update the policy rollout runbook — add a 15m canary wait and a circuit-breaker that auto-rolls-back if `warm_pool_size` drops >5% in 10m.

lina_cost: also propose a soft cap: if warm-pool < 90% and autoscaler is launching >10 nodes in 10m, pause non-critical canary rollouts for security changes to avoid cascading costs.

mike_sre: agree. For immediate mitigation, I've added a temporary runbook entry to increase warm-pool headroom by 10% during policy rollouts for keystore or privnet changes.

sara: action owners captured. Can we mark incident severity as P2? We lost capacity but didn't affect serving (mostly onboarding warm pool).

anika_sec: P2 ack. Will coordinate with compliance to ensure audit trail of the rollback. I already saved the policy diff in `s3://redwood-audit/policy-rollbacks/4725123456.diff`.

kenny_oncall: filing incident for postmortem. Please add timestamps and reproduce steps if anyone runs the rollback test.

devon_platform: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/node-agent/pull/1423 — includes fallback, metrics, and unit tests. Requesting review from @mike_sre and @anika_sec.

mike_sre: reviewing now. Also adding a short-term alert rule: `sum(increase(node_boot_failures[5m])) by (az) > 3 and sum(increase(keystore_403[5m])) by (az) > 5` -> page oncall.

lina_cost: FYI I'll annotate the cost dashboard for the hour so finance sees the bump and we can link to the postmortem.

sara: thanks team. closing out once devon gets reviewers and canary test passes in staging. :thumbsup:
